note: Ground truth for the intake helper, batch_a. Written by hand from the guideline documents, before any tool run. expected_rules lists the rules a person reading the document would confirm (or, where marked proposed, would leave unconfirmed). key_params are the values stated in the document. Keyword lists (vague phrases, clerical phrases, overhead phrases and codes, AI terms) are NOT ground truth and are left out of key_params: see README. sentences_that_are_not_rules are sentences an intake pass must not turn into a rule of the type named.
scoring_suggestion: A proposed rule matches when its type matches and its source sentence overlaps the source_quote. Score type recall and precision first, then key_params equality on matched rules. Severity is the test author's judgement and should be reported separately, not counted as wrong.

expected_rules.source_quote: Only people the claims examiner has cleared in writing for the claim.
One attorney paid per deposition, mediation, arbitration session or court hearing; a second needs the examiner's OK beforehand.
Capped at 0.2 hr per entry, per person.
Six-minute units (0.1 hr); no quarter hours.
A timekeeper with 80% or more of entries (6 entries minimum) landing on the half hour or the hour gets audited.
Each entry covers a single task with its own time; lumped entries are cut.
Say what was done and to what; "attention to file", "follow up" and similar get zero.
Task code and activity code on fee lines, expense code on cost lines; all mandatory.
Over 9.0 hrs by one person in one day is not paid without a written reason.
Work more than 75 days old at invoice date is not paid.
Same entry twice: the second one is struck.
The approved rate sheet for the claim is the ceiling.
45 days' written notice to the examiner before a new rate may be billed.
Secretarial and file-room work; training and onboarding; conflicts clearance; preparing or fixing bills.
Up to 2.5 hrs per claim without asking; beyond that, examiner pre-approval.
Paid at half the approved rate.
Not reimbursed: postage, word processing, local telephone, office supplies.
Required for any single charge of $35.00 or more.
Meals max $55.00 per person per day; hotel max $190.00 per night.
At cost, no uplift.

sentences_that_are_not_rules.text: Quarterly, or at $5,000 of unbilled time, whichever comes first.
sentences_that_are_not_rules.why: invoice frequency; no rule type covers it
a per-page copy rate; no rule type covers it. It must not be read as a per diem cap or a receipt threshold

sentences_that_are_not_rules.text: Status report to the examiner every 90 days.
sentences_that_are_not_rules.why: a reporting duty; the 90 days must not be read as a late-time limit or a rate notice period

expected_rules.source_quote: the aggregate of all fees and costs invoiced on a matter shall at no time surpass the maximum compensation set out in the applicable engagement letter unless and until the Board has approved an increase by written amendment.

Where the engagement letter divides the maximum compensation among phases of work, Counsel shall not invoice against any phase a sum greater than the portion assigned to that phase, it being understood that savings in one phase do not carry over to another without the General Manager's written consent.
Hourly rates are those appearing in the fee schedule attached to the engagement letter, and no timekeeper shall be billed at a rate higher than the rate there shown for that timekeeper.
The District will not pay for the time of any person who does not appear by name in the fee schedule.
Absent the General Manager's prior written consent, not more than four (4) timekeepers shall record time to a single matter in any one billing month.
All time shall be kept contemporaneously and stated in units of one-tenth (0.1) of an hour.

Each entry shall be confined to one activity; an entry exceeding one and one-half (1.5) hours that aggregates distinct activities under a single time figure will be disallowed in its entirety, the District being unable to assess the reasonableness of the time devoted to each.
Every time entry shall bear the task code corresponding to the phase of work to which it relates.
Time submitted more than one hundred twenty (120) days after the date on which the work was performed is deemed waived.
Counsel shall review each invoice before submission to ensure that no service appears on it more than once; any repeated entry will be deducted.
Time spent in transit is compensable only where the General Counsel has authorized the trip in writing before it is taken; authorized transit time is paid at the timekeeper's ordinary rate.
The hourly rates are understood to absorb the cost of secretarial support, filing, photocopying, calendaring and similar administrative functions, none of which shall appear as a time charge.
Subsistence while away overnight on District business is reimbursable up to forty dollars ($40.00) per person per day for meals and one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) per night for lodging.
Counsel shall furnish a receipt for every cost item in excess of $20.00.
Costs advanced to third parties on the District's behalf shall be invoiced in the amount actually paid, without surcharge or handling fee.

sentences_that_are_not_rules.text: The District does not impose a ceiling on the number of hours a timekeeper may record in a single day, but Counsel should expect questions where the hours recorded appear disproportionate to the task.
sentences_that_are_not_rules.why: says there is NO daily limit; a daily_hour_cap rule must not be proposed from it

sentences_that_are_not_rules.text: Invoices shall be rendered monthly and addressed to the General Manager, and shall be paid within forty-five (45) days of receipt.
sentences_that_are_not_rules.why: payment terms; the 45 days is not a late-time limit or a rate notice period

sentences_that_are_not_rules.text: Counsel shall maintain professional liability coverage of not less than $2,000,000 throughout the engagement.

expected_rules.source_quote: Quarter-hour increments (0.25) are fine with us, just be consistent about it.
Please don't cram a whole afternoon into one line: two related tasks in an entry is OK, but if an entry of more than an hour lists three or more things I'll send it back to be split.
Tell me what you actually did, because "work on matter" or "review file" tells me nothing and I can't approve it.
If any one person bills more than 10 hours in a day I'm going to ask why, so give me a heads-up.
For hearings and depositions, two of your lawyers at most on our dime.
Internal meetings among your own team: bill up to half an hour (0.5) per entry and no more.
Clear it with me before the team spends more than 6 hours on legal research on a matter.
Whatever is on the rate schedule we signed in January is the rate, and nothing above it.
Anything older than 60 days when the bill goes out, we won't pay.
If a line shows up twice, we pay it once.
Please don't pass through overhead: online research subscriptions, phones, postage, staff overtime, word processing.
Vendor costs come through at what you paid, with no markup.
put "(GenAI)" in the narrative of any time entry where one was used.
We won't pay lawyer rates for AI-written summaries or digests of depositions and documents, or for AI doing the first-level document review.
Honestly we'd rather not pay for travel time at all, but I haven't settled that with our CFO yet, so treat it as a preference for now and let's talk before any big trip.

sentences_that_are_not_rules.text: Last thing: please get bills to me by the 5th of the month and copy accounts payable.
sentences_that_are_not_rules.why: bill timing; no rule type covers it
